PMID:41807022.topic: Shared decision making and patient information documentation for joint replacement
PMID:41807022.setting: Elective orthopaedic (preoperative) clinics, University Hospital of North Tees, district general hospital (secondary care)
PMID:41807022.standard: NICE NG157 and GIRFT Elective Hip and Knee Pathway: documentation of patient information leaflet provision and shared decision making domains (no numerical target stated)

cycle1.result: PIL offered documented in 7% (hip) and 9% (knee); consent form copy given 30% (hip) and 50% (knee); understanding and willingness to proceed 79% (hip) and 73% (knee); recovery expectations, spinal anaesthetic and wound care ≤9%.

PMID:41807022.intervention: QR code-linked digital patient information leaflet (procedure, recovery, anaesthetic options, wound care, translation links) given at the end of clinic; staff encouraged to offer it and document its provision.

cycle2.result: PIL offered documented in 24% (hip) and 36% (knee); understanding and willingness to proceed 90% (hip) and 100% (knee); recovery expectations, spinal anaesthetic and wound care up to 36%; consent form copy 28% (hip) and 50% (knee).

PMID:41807022.other_findings: Documentation of a consent form copy did not improve. Patient survey: 100% found the digital information clear, 86% preferred it to paper and 71% felt more engaged.

PMID:30596799.setting: Trauma-receiving NHS hospitals in England (TARN registry)

cycle1.result: Registry analysis: 3,792 deaths at 30 days; deprivation not associated with major trauma mortality; for minor trauma the most and second most deprived had aORs 1.35 and 1.28 for 30-day mortality.

PMID:30596799.other_findings: Thirty-day mortality was 10% in patients over 85 with minor trauma, higher than major trauma in all age groups under 65.

PMID:36670302.topic: Hospital volume and hip fracture care quality
PMID:36670302.setting: 68 hospitals in the nationwide Dutch Hip Fracture Audit

cycle1.result: Registry association study: surgery within 48 h 92.3%, orthogeriatric co-treatment 77.3%, 30-day mortality 5.6% overall; volume not associated with mortality; orthogeriatric co-treatment rose with volume up to 367 patients per year then fell (p < 0.01).

PMID:36670302.other_findings: No clinically relevant relation between hospital volume and time in the emergency department, surgery within 48 h or length of stay.

PMID:34873533.setting: Jordan University Hospital, Amman, tertiary academic hospital; elective orthopaedic surgery records
PMID:34873533.standard: Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (STAR), based on Royal College of Surgeons guidance on medical record keeping (no target stated)
PMID:34873533.intervention: Annual teaching of practitioners on documentation using slides based on Royal College of Surgeons of England recommendations, with periodic (annual) re-auditing.
PMID:34873533.other_findings: Yearly audits 2016–2021 (454 records) showed scores of 95.5, 95.9, 95.7 and 96.8 for 2017–2020; consent and anaesthetic domains plateaued. Benefits on the consent form and post-op instructions were never documented, and suture details fell to 41.5%.

PMID:40975842.topic: Corridor care in hip fracture patients
PMID:40975842.setting: Ashford and St Peter's NHS Foundation Trust; NHS hospital participating in the National Hip Fracture Database

cycle1.result: Cross-sectional study: 11% cared for in nondesignated areas; ≥1 h 20 min in such areas associated with ≥3 ward moves (OR 4.02, 1.61–10.06); orthogeriatric ward LOS 13.4 days for bed care vs 17.2 days for >4 h 20 min.

PMID:40975842.other_findings: Care in nondesignated areas peaked in winter (44.6%). Multiple ward moves (OR 2.63) and prolonged LOS (OR 3.23) were associated with higher in-hospital mortality.

PMID:42082282.setting: Major trauma centre (two hospital sites), University Hospitals Birmingham; distal radius fracture ORIF
PMID:42082282.standard: BOAST 'The Safe Use of Intraoperative Tourniquets' (2021): documentation of seven parameters (time, skin condition, padding, site, compressive exsanguination, pressure, size)

cycle1.result: Tourniquet pressure 20.5% (7/34), time 55.9% (19/34); site, padding, exsanguination, skin condition and size all 0%.

PMID:42082282.intervention: Teaching session for junior doctors and theatre staff, a three-part tourniquet safety checklist in theatres, and BOAST posters in theatre preparation areas.

cycle2.result: Pressure 59.0% (37/63), site 32.0% (20), padding 14.0% (9), exsanguination 13.0% (8), skin condition 11.0% (7), size 10.0% (6), time 56.0% (35).

PMID:42082282.other_findings: Tourniquet time did not improve and most parameters stayed below 50%. Checklist uptake was not captured; mandatory electronic operative note fields are planned.

PMID:39759656.topic: Confusion and vitamin D screening in hip fracture
PMID:39759656.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics Department, Royal Shrewsbury Hospital, district general hospital
PMID:39759656.standard: Confusion screening (AMTS) and vitamin D testing within 24 hours of admission in hip fracture patients aged 60 and over (no target stated)

cycle1.result: 27/100 (27%) screened; 14/27 (51.85%) of screens done within 24 hours.

PMID:39759656.intervention: Educational sessions for clinicians, nurses and ancillary staff, posters, email reminders and screening prompts added to the admission checklist (July 2023).
PMID:39759656.other_findings: Abnormal vitamin D levels stayed high (56% then 55%). Many patients with normal AMTS still had abnormal confusion screens.

PMID:40542998.setting: Dietetic Orthopaedic Physiotherapy Screening Clinic, Mater South Brisbane, tertiary metropolitan hospital outpatient clinic

cycle1.result: Descriptive chart audit: 32% achieved clinically significant weight loss (>5%), 58% no change, 11% gained weight; mean 182 days in care and 5 appointments per patient.

PMID:40542998.other_findings: 50% of the weight loss group had a very low energy diet vs 19% of the no weight loss group (p = 0.05). Only 12% of those discharged reached goal weight.

PMID:38827564.topic: Female representation in Achilles repair research
PMID:38827564.setting: Literature review of PubMed studies on operative Achilles repair

cycle1.result: Female representation 1783 of 10,673 subjects (16.7%) across 169 studies; 5.0% in studies of world-class athletes.

PMID:38827564.other_findings: 32 male-only vs 3 female-only studies; no study collected menstrual status data.

PMID:37250580.setting: UK national trainee-led trauma and orthopaedic collaborative projects

cycle1.result: 10 trainee-led collaborative projects identified during the COVID-19 lockdown (none in 2019); 6 published, levels of evidence 3 to 4.

PMID:37250580.other_findings: Five audits and five cohort studies; recruitment mostly via social media and data collection mostly via REDCap.

PMID:26470676.topic: Inpatient falls risk assessment and prevention
PMID:26470676.setting: Calvary Wakefield Hospital, private acute hospital, medical and surgical wards
PMID:26470676.standard: Hospital Falls Minimization Program and National Safety and Quality Health Service Standard 10 (Preventing Falls and Harm from Falls); eight JBI audit criteria

cycle1.result: Baseline audit showed significant opportunity for improvement in all criteria (figures not given in abstract).

PMID:26470676.intervention: Corrective action plan after the baseline audit (details not given in abstract).

cycle2.dates: Six months after the implementation phase
cycle2.result: Results were maintained and consistent with the first follow-up audit (figures not given in abstract).

PMID:26470676.other_findings: At the first follow-up (three months), nearly all criteria improved; formal staff education improved by 46% and patient and family education by 43%.

PMID:25151180.topic: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block in the emergency department
PMID:25151180.setting: Emergency and Trauma Centre, The Alfred Hospital, Melbourne
PMID:25151180.standard: Evidence-based use of nerve blocks and multimodal analgesia for older patients with neck of femur fracture (no target stated)
PMID:25151180.intervention: Educational and awareness strategies on pain management for emergency department clinical staff.

cycle2.result: Significant increase in nerve block use and multimodal analgesia and a reduction in average milligrams of morphine given (figures not given in abstract).

PMID:25151180.other_findings: Title also reports improved triage and assessment; abstract gives no numbers.
